items.followUp: Differentiate between a saturated solution and an unsaturated solution.

rubric.why: Identifies a dilute solution by its relatively low solute content.
rubric.description: States that a dilute solution contains a small amount of solute relative to the solvent or solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct comparison.

rubric.why: Identifies a concentrated solution by its relatively high solute content.
rubric.description: States that a concentrated solution contains a large amount of solute relative to the solvent or solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct comparison.

modelAnswer: A dilute solution contains a small amount of solute relative to the amount of solvent or solution.
A concentrated solution contains a large amount of solute relative to the amount of solvent or solution.

items.followUp: Differentiate between an atom and an atomic ion, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: Defines a molecule by its neutrality and bonded atoms.
rubric.description: Defines a molecule as a neutral group of two or more chemically bonded atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a definition that includes neutrality and chemically bonded atoms.

rubric.why: Provides a correct example of a neutral molecule.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable example of a molecule, such as H₂O or O₂.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example.

rubric.why: Defines a molecular ion as bonded atoms with an overall charge.
rubric.description: States that a molecular ion is a group of bonded atoms carrying an overall positive or negative charge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining the charged group of bonded atoms.

rubric.why: Provides a correct example of a molecular ion.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable example of a molecular ion, such as NH₄⁺, SO₄²⁻ or NO₃⁻.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example.

modelAnswer: A molecule is a neutral group of two or more atoms chemically bonded together; for example, H₂O.
A molecular ion is a group of bonded atoms carrying an overall charge; for example, NH₄⁺.

items.followUp: Define an ionic bond and explain how it forms in sodium chloride.

accept: one or more pairs of electrons
rubric.why: States the defining feature of covalent bonding.
rubric.description: Defines a covalent bond as a bond formed when atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for a correct definition that identifies atoms sharing electron pair(s).

rubric.why: Identifies a single bond, the number of shared pairs, and an example.
rubric.description: Explains that a single covalent bond involves sharing one pair of electrons and gives an example such as H₂ or Cl₂.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the type, one shared pair, and a correct example.

rubric.why: Identifies a double bond, the number of shared pairs, and an example.
rubric.description: Explains that a double covalent bond involves sharing two pairs of electrons and gives an example such as O₂.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the type, two shared pairs, and a correct example.

rubric.why: Identifies a triple bond, the number of shared pairs, and an example.
rubric.description: Explains that a triple covalent bond involves sharing three pairs of electrons and gives an example such as N₂.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the type, three shared pairs, and a correct example.

modelAnswer: A covalent bond is formed when atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.
A single covalent bond involves sharing one pair of electrons; for example, H₂.
A double covalent bond involves sharing two pairs of electrons; for example, O₂.
A triple covalent bond involves sharing three pairs of electrons; for example, N₂.

items.followUp: Define boiling point and explain how it is affected by atmospheric pressure.

rubric.why: Gives the equilibrium definition of vapour pressure.
rubric.description: Defines vapour pressure as the pressure exerted by a vapour in equilibrium with its liquid at a given temperature.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the definition including pressure, vapour, liquid, and equilibrium.

rubric.why: States the effect of temperature on vapour pressure.
rubric.description: Explains that vapour pressure increases as temperature increases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct trend.

rubric.why: States how the strength of intermolecular forces affects vapour pressure.
rubric.description: Explains that weaker intermolecular forces give higher vapour pressure, while stronger forces give lower vapour pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct relationship between intermolecular-force strength and vapour pressure.

modelAnswer: Vapour pressure is the pressure exerted by a vapour in equilibrium with its liquid at a given temperature.
Vapour pressure increases as the temperature increases.
The nature of the liquid also affects vapour pressure: weaker intermolecular forces give a higher vapour pressure, while stronger forces give a lower vapour pressure.

items.followUp: What are alkali metals? Describe how their reactivity changes down Group 1.

rubric.why: Identifies the group containing the halogens.
rubric.description: States that halogens are the elements of Group VIIA (Group 17).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the group.

rubric.why: States the characteristic nature and molecular form of halogens.
rubric.description: States that halogens are non-metals and occur as diatomic molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when both properties are stated.

rubric.why: Explains the electron-gain process by which halogens act as oxidizing agents.
rubric.description: States that halogens gain electrons to form halide ions, thereby oxidizing other substances.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the electron-gain and halide-ion explanation.

rubric.why: Gives the correct order of oxidizing strength.
rubric.description: States that oxidizing power decreases down the group: F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct order.

modelAnswer: Halogens are the non-metal elements of Group VIIA (Group 17); they occur as diatomic molecules.
Halogens are oxidizing agents because their atoms gain electrons to form halide ions.
Their oxidizing power decreases down the group: F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂.
